title: Freddy's wish to be Duke Ellington; the band never paid
summary: Briggs says Johnson wanted to front the Harlemites as Ellington did and was taking money for himself, bookings in Belgium and Holland were cancelled, and the musicians never got paid for recordings.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, it was Freddie's leadership? Freddie was the leader?
Yes. It was Arthur Briggs -- Freddie Johnson and then Arthur Briggs, but you have to have one man fronting, you see.
Right.

Freddie's intention was to more or less, to imitate Duke Ellington, but he couldn't, because Duke Ellington built his band around him. And that's a different thing, you see.
Duke Ellington's band without -- with another piano player, wouldn't sound the same way.
Right.
It's just the same as Count Basie's orchestra with another piano
Briggs
player, it wouldn't sound the same way, you see.
Right.
And Freddie had had the same idea of being a Duke Ellington, and having the Harlemites around him, but it wasn't -- it couldn't be the same, you see.
And after Sterling Conaway found out what was going on, the majority of the boys said they're not going to quit their jobs to take a chance on a wild goose chase, you see.

And, we had several engagements in Belgium and Holland, and every place else, that had to be cancelled. I don't know whether Canetti had to pay a duty -- or they had to pay a fine or something, I don't know.
But, it didn't interest me, because in the way that they had arranged the contract, that he and Freddie -- Conaway said that he had heard Freddie telling his wife; he said,
Briggs
"Darling, when I come back, that trunk will be stacked with 1,000 franc bills," you see.
Yes, I see.
And that's the wrong way. If you're going to do something together, do it together or not.
Surely, Freddy wanted to make some money. We all wanted to make some money. We were thinking of making a reputation doing something.
But he thought of one thing, just knocking out everybody, and taking everything for himself. That was all, with Canetti.
Well, this band -- in other words, even when it wasn't just the records, but when you were on the road, you were getting just a share -- and you never really knew what the.--
Yes, yes. And I'll tell you something about the recording. We never got a dime.
Briggs
You never got a dime?
Not a dime. My satisfaction is to listen to the recordings. (Laughter).
Right. Well, it sounds as if Canetti was a bit shrewd; right.
Yes, he was. And Freddy was with him. They worked together.
I see.
